Read the whole post before applying.This is not make-a-mood-board-and-watch. You'll be publishing real content under our name, running real campaigns with real budgets behind them, and owning numbers that leadership actually looks at. Real deadlines, real consequences, with the Marketing Manager beside you and modern AI tooling at your back. The pace is fast and the standard is high. You'll learn more here in a few months than in a year anywhere else, because we hand you real responsibility and expect you to rise to it. Hard on purpose. If that sounds like too much, this is the wrong post.We need an absolute ninja. Someone who comes in, learns how the marketing engine actually works, and takes ownership of pieces of it with due time.You'll doContent and channelsWrite across everything we publish: blog posts, emails, landing pages, social content, campaign copy. What you write goes live.Support SEO research, format and optimize blog content, and build and maintain website pages.Schedule and publish across our social channels, then track what performs and say why.Engage physician conversations across forums, social platforms, and the communities where our audience already spends time. You'll be speaking as the firm, so precision matters.Build graphics and marketing assets to support campaigns across channels.Campaigns and operationsEmail: build and proof campaigns before they go out, manage list segmentation, and catch the typo before ten thousand physicians see it.Paid media: support campaign assets, pull performance data, and track results against goals.Partnerships: track deliverables across partner programs and keep co-branded content moving. Nobody chases you; you chase them.Events and webinars: promotional assets, registration pages, post-event follow-up.Analytics: keep tracking and attribution clean, build regular performance reports, and dig into what's working and what isn't. When a number looks wrong, find out why before someone asks.Research: track competitors and market trends, and surface what's worth acting on.Growth projects: help launch channels and platforms we don't have yet.Use AI and automation so your reps go to judgment, not busywork.Who this is forThe sharpest person in your program. Learns fast, works hard without being told twice, energized by a heavy workload. Three things we care about most:Writing. You write clean, tight copy that doesn't need a rewrite before it ships. You know the difference between words that fill space and words that move someone. Be ready to show a writing sample or write something on the spot.Detail. Marketing looks polished or sloppy based entirely on the small things: the broken link, the wrong UTM, the subject line that renders badly on mobile. You catch these before they go out, not after.Numbers and follow-through. You think in steps and notice when something doesn't add up. A campaign's attribution is off, a partner deliverable is nine days late, two reports disagree on last month's leads. You catch it and say something instead of moving on.And be honest with yourself about the manual work. A lot of this is scheduling, formatting, data cleanup, and tracking spreadsheets. It is not always interesting. It still has to be right, because everything downstream depends on it. If tedious-but-important work drains you, this is not the right seat.This is not for anyone who needs hand-holding or wants a comfortable lane.Boundary on scope: anything carrying real brand or spend exposure (budget decisions, public statements on tax positions, partner commitments) is yours to prepare and the Marketing Manager's to decide. You will never be left holding that alone.The path: Perform and you convert to full-time, then keep climbing. Earned, not given.Selection: We screen hard. Very few who apply are selected. If you're the right person, that should make you want this more.Details$14 to $20 an hour, 30 to 40 hours per week.Fully remote.Year-round, running through until you graduate.A flexible schedule built around your classes.RequirementsPursuing a degree in marketing or a related program.Strong written communication. Be ready to prove it.Organized, accurate, fast. Comfortable in spreadsheets and picking up new tools and platforms quickly.Familiar with marketing channels and how they connect to each other.Curious about a niche industry. Physician tax is more interesting than it sounds.Prior marketing experience is a plus: an internship, a class project, a club, or something you built yourself.Hungry to grow into a full-time role and own it.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Marketing Intern at Doc Wealth
jobs.description: Employer: Doc Wealth Expires: 09/03/2026 Marketing Intern (Year-Round, Path to Full-Time)We're building the largest physician-focused tax company in the country, growing faster than anyone in this space. This role sits inside the marketing team and touches everything: what we publish, what we spend, and whether the growth engine actually compounds. Read the whole post before applying.This is not make-a-mood-board-and-watch. You'll be publishing real content under our name, running real campaigns with real budgets behind them, and owning numbers that leadership actually looks at. Real deadlines, real consequences, with the Marketing Manager beside you and modern AI tooling at your back. The pace is fast and the standard is high. You'll learn more here in a few months than in a year anywhere else, because we hand you real responsibility and expect you to rise to it. Hard on purpose. If that sounds like too much, this is the wrong post.We need an absolute ninja. Someone who comes in, learns how the marketing engine actually works, and takes ownership of pieces of it with due time.You'll doContent and channelsWrite across everything we publish: blog posts, emails, landing pages, social content, campaign copy. What you write goes live.Support SEO research, format and optimize blog content, and build and maintain website pages.Schedule and publish across our social channels, then track what performs and say why.Engage physician conversations across forums, social platforms, and the communities where our audience already spends time. You'll be speaking as the firm, so precision matters.Build graphics and marketing assets to support campaigns across channels.Campaigns and operationsEmail: build and proof campaigns before they go out, manage list segmentation, and catch the typo before ten thousand physicians see it.Paid media: support campaign assets, pull performance data, and track results against goals.Partnerships: track deliverables across partner programs and keep co-branded content moving. Nobody chases you; you chase them.Events and webinars: promotional assets, registration pages, post-event follow-up.Analytics: keep tracking and attribution clean, build regular performance reports, and dig into what's working and what isn't. When a number looks wrong, find out why before someone asks.Research: track competitors and market trends, and surface what's worth acting on.Growth projects: help launch channels and platforms we don't have yet.Use AI and automation so your reps go to judgment, not busywork.Who this is forThe sharpest person in your program. Learns fast, works hard without being told twice, energized by a heavy workload. Three things we care about most:Writing. You write clean, tight copy that doesn't need a rewrite before it ships. You know the difference between words that fill space and words that move someone. Be ready to show a writing sample or write something on the spot.Detail. Marketing looks polished or sloppy based entirely on the small things: the broken link, the wrong UTM, the subject line that renders badly on mobile. You catch these before they go out, not after.Numbers and follow-through. You think in steps and notice when something doesn't add up. A campaign's attribution is off, a partner deliverable is nine days late, two reports disagree on last month's leads. You catch it and say something instead of moving on.And be honest with yourself about the manual work. A lot of this is scheduling, formatting, data cleanup, and tracking spreadsheets. It is not always interesting. It still has to be right, because everything downstream depends on it. If tedious-but-important work drains you, this is not the right seat.This is not for anyone who needs hand-holding or wants a comfortable lane.Boundary on scope: anything carrying real brand or spend exposure (budget decisions, public statements on tax positions, partner commitments) is yours to prepare and the Marketing Manager's to decide. You will never be left holding that alone.The path: Perform and you convert to full-time, then keep climbing. Earned, not given.Selection: We screen hard. Very few who apply are selected. If you're the right person, that should make you want this more.Details$14 to $20 an hour, 30 to 40 hours per week.Fully remote.Year-round, running through until you graduate.A flexible schedule built around your classes.RequirementsPursuing a degree in marketing or a related program.Strong written communication. Be ready to prove it.Organized, accurate, fast. Comfortable in spreadsheets and picking up new tools and platforms quickly.Familiar with marketing channels and how they connect to each other.Curious about a niche industry. Physician tax is more interesting than it sounds.Prior marketing experience is a plus: an internship, a class project, a club, or something you built yourself.Hungry to grow into a full-time role and own it.

jobs.title: Data and AI Intern at 11:11 Media
jobs.description: Employer: 11:11 Media Expires: 09/03/2026 11:11 Media Data and AI Intern - Fall 2026 Overview of the Company11:11 Media is a global next-gen media company, founded by Paris Hilton. 11:11 Media operates at the center of pop culture – connecting content, community and commerce, spanning a broad array of businesses, including film, TV, audio, music, books, consumer products, and digital, with passion points around lifestyle, fashion, beauty, wellness, art, travel and more. Elevating brands, building communities, and driving social impact through the power of storytelling, experiences, and products is the core mission of 11:11 Media.About the RoleWe are seeking a Data & AI Intern to help our team turn data into faster decisions, smarter operations, and scalable AI-powered workflows across 11:11 Media. In this role, you’ll work hand in hand with our team on real projects that improve how we understand business performance, uncover insights and opportunities, and automate recurring processes across the entire company, including: commerce, marketing, media, brand partnerships, finance, and operations. This is a dual-mode role. You'll be in strategic conversations — helping shape how we think about a problem, what questions are worth asking, and what good looks like — and then you'll be the one building the answer. The ideal candidate moves naturally between both modes and sees them as connected, not separate.Analytics & InsightsAnalyze data across key business lines while surfacing trends, anomalies, and opportunities.Assist with data labeling, preprocessing, and feature engineering in support of machine learning workflowsSupport ongoing reporting and ad hoc requests with high-quality, repeatable outputsDashboards, KPIs & MeasurementBuild and maintain data pipelines that extract, structure, and connect data across business systems to support both analytics and AI initiativesBuild and improve dashboards and self-serve reporting that teams can trust and use.Partner with department leads to standardize, maintain and enhance KPIs and measurement frameworksAI + Automation (Practical, Shipped Work)Prototype, implement, and evaluate AI-enabled workflows, tools, and frameworks (e.g., deploy GPTs, bots, and automations).Identify repeatable processes and convert them into lightweight tools, templates, or automations.Rapidly prototype AI tools and agents, iterating quickly based on real user feedbackProcess & Systems ImprovementPartner with teams to streamline how data is collected, organized, and utilized.Collaborate with cross-functional teams to validate AI outputs against real-world business scenariosDocument workflows, processes, and best practices to support scaling and knowledge transfer across the teamThe InternshipApplication Deadline: August 14, 2026Term length: September 2026 - December 2026, with the possibility of extension.Workplace Type: This is an onsite role based out of our LA/Beverly Hills office.Schedule: A part-time, flexible schedule working 20 - 25 hours per week. Compensation: $25.00 - $35.00 per hourWhat’s in it for youYour work ships fast and matters immediately - this isn't a "shadow and observe" internship. You'll be building dashboards, automations, and analyses that real teams use to make real decisions in real time. The feedback loop is short, the stakes are real, and the impact is visible.You'll work at the center of culture, not adjacent to it - 11:11 Media sits at the intersection of entertainment, commerce, fashion, beauty, and wellness. The data you work with reflects what audiences are watching, buying, wearing, and talking about right now. Data isn't a back-office function here - it's how we operate - insights and analytics are core to how 11:11 makes decisions across every business line, from content to brand partnerships to commerce. You won't be building reports no one reads. You'll be in the room (or Slack thread) where it gets used.You'll work with people who are exceptional at what they do - our team combines deep expertise across media, business, and technology with a genuine culture of collaboration and creative ambition. You'll learn a lot, quickly, from people who care about doing great work.You'll build a portfolio that actually means something - by the end of the term, you'll have real, shipped work to show: dashboards, automations, analysis templates, or internal tooling with measurable business impact. Not slide decks about hypothetical projects.You'll get a rare window into how a successful media and commerce business really works - from content strategy to brand partnerships to consumer products, you'll see how data connects across the full operation and gain context most analysts don't get until years into their careers.You'll work alongside one of the world's most iconic entrepreneurs - Paris Hilton isn't just a figurehead here. 11:11 Media is her vision, and the work you do will directly support it. The team around her is world-class, and the culture they've built is collaborative, kind, and genuinely inclusive.What you will Bring to the RoleCurrently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program (Business, Marketing, Commerce, Economics or similar preferred).Deep knowledge and practical application of AI tools and automation (you build things that get used and make other’s lives easier).Strong analytical thinking and comfort working through ambiguity.Experience working with data (spreadsheets, BI tools, SQL, Python/R, or similar).Experience with visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI)Interpersonal communication, written, and presentation skills—able to explain findings to non-technical audiences.Ownership mindset and attention to detail.Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple tasksHigh emotional intelligence and a self-starter, positive attitudeThe expected salary range for this position is $25.00 - $35.00 per hour. Our Company provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression. We deeply understand the value of bringing together a team with different perspectives, educational backgrounds, and life experiences. We encourage people from underrepresented backgrounds to apply. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other marginalized folks tend to only apply when they check every box. So if you think you have what it takes, but don't necessarily meet every single point on the job description, please still get in touch. We'd love to have a chat and see if you could be a great addition to our team.

jobs.description: Employer: The Brave Women's Community Theatre Expires: 09/09/2026 Development, Fundraising & Community Partnerships InternshipFall 2026 Semester (August – December) or Spring Semester (January 2027 – May 2027)Location: Lakewood, Colorado (Hybrid) | Hours: Approximately 8–10 hours per week (flexible) | Compensation: $300 stipend Help Build Something That MattersJoin a growing nonprofit dedicated to helping women heal from interpersonal abuse through creativity, connection, and community. This internship offers a unique opportunity to help build the foundation of an organization making a meaningful impact in the lives of survivors while gaining hands-on experience in nonprofit development, fundraising, community partnerships, and organizational growth. About The Brave Women's Community CenterThe Brave Women's Community Center (BWCC) is a Colorado nonprofit that provides trauma-informed, evidence-informed creative and relational programming for women who have experienced interpersonal abuse. Through expressive arts, storytelling, peer support, and community-centered programming, BWCC helps women rebuild self-trust, strengthen resilience, and create meaningful connections. As a growing nonprofit, BWCC offers interns the opportunity to make a tangible impact while gaining hands-on experience in nonprofit leadership, fundraising, community partnerships, and organizational development. Our MissionThe Brave Women's Community Center supports women who have experienced interpersonal abuse by providing trauma-informed, evidence-informed creative and relational programming. Through expressive arts, peer-based support, and structured group experiences, we help participants recognize harmful patterns, rebuild self-trust, and strengthen resilience. Our work complements crisis intervention and clinical services by offering restorative, preventative spaces where women can foster connection, reclaim their agency, and build the foundation for long-term healing. About the InternshipThe Development, Fundraising & Community Partnerships Intern will work closely with the Executive Director to help strengthen the long-term sustainability of The Brave Women's Community Center. This position is ideal for a student interested in nonprofit leadership, fundraising, business development, marketing, or community engagement who wants meaningful, hands-on experience helping a mission-driven organization grow.The intern will assist in identifying funding opportunities, cultivating community partnerships, researching prospective donors and sponsors, and supporting fundraising initiatives that expand BWCC's impact throughout Colorado. ResponsibilitiesThe Development, Fundraising & Community Partnerships Intern may assist with:Researching prospective individual donors, corporate sponsors, and foundations that align with BWCC's missionBuilding and organizing donor, sponsor, and community partner prospect listsResearching grant opportunities and assisting with grant preparationIdentifying speaking opportunities, conferences, networking events, and community outreach opportunitiesAssisting with sponsorship packages for programs, events, and the Brave Hearts Speak podcastSupporting Colorado Gives campaigns and other fundraising initiativesResearching employer matching gift programs and donor-advised fund opportunitiesHelping develop outreach materials, donor communications, and partnership presentationsAssisting in organizing fundraising strategies and relationship management systemsParticipating in community meetings, networking events, and partnership development as appropriateContributing ideas that strengthen BWCC's long-term sustainability and community impact Preferred QualificationsIdeal majors include:Business AdministrationMarketingNonprofit ManagementEntrepreneurshipCommunicationsPublic RelationsManagementFinanceSalesOr a related fieldStudents from other majors with a passion for nonprofit work, community impact, and social change are encouraged to apply. What You'll GainThis internship offers an opportunity to:Gain meaningful experience in nonprofit leadership and organizational developmentLearn about fundraising strategy, donor engagement, and community partnershipsBuild professional communication and relationship-building skillsDevelop experience with grant research, sponsorships, and nonprofit sustainabilityWork directly with the Executive Director of a growing nonprofitBuild a portfolio of real-world nonprofit development projectsMake a meaningful impact in the lives of women recovering from interpersonal abuse About the FounderLucia Severtson, MA, LPC, R-DMT, is the Founder and Executive Director of The Brave Women's Community Center. She is a Licensed Professional Counselor and Registered Dance/Movement Therapist with nearly two decades of experience working with women recovering from trauma, anxiety, OCD, and interpersonal abuse. Lucia is passionate about combining evidence-based mental health practices with creativity, storytelling, movement, theatre, and community to foster healing. She is also the host of the Brave Hearts Speak podcast, where survivors share their stories of resilience to inspire hope and healing in others. How to ApplyPlease submit the following:ResumeCover Letter describing your interest in BWCC's mission and this internshipEmail: Lucia@bravewomenscommunity.comSubject Line: Development Internship Application – Your Name

jobs.title: B2B Sales & Marketing Internship at Altitude Promotions
jobs.description: Employer: Altitude Promotions Expires: 09/12/2026 The Sales & Marketing Internship at Altitude Promotions offers a fast-paced, hands-on introduction to the world of B2B sales and marketing. Interns gain real-world experience representing Fortune 500 clients, managing professional relationships with business owners, and learning how to drive revenue growth through strategic marketing and sales initiatives. As part of being an intern at Altitude Promotions, interns will work closely with various teams across the company — including Sales, Public Relations, and Human Resources — to gain a full understanding of how different departments operate together to achieve company goals. Interns start by learning the fundamentals of sales: building client relationships, communicating value, and developing confidence through direct interaction with businesses. However, the goal isn’t to stay in sales — it’s to use that experience as a launchpad for growth into broader roles in marketing, management, or leadership. Altitude Promotions emphasizes personal and professional development, helping interns strengthen their communication, teamwork, and strategic skills so they can transition into positions that align with their long-term career ambitions. Key ResponsibilitiesRepresent Fortune 500 clients in direct sales and marketing campaigns.Develop and implement marketing strategies tailored to local and regional markets.Generate leads, qualify prospects, and close sales through effective relationship-building and communication.Collaborate with senior leadership to analyze campaign performance and identify opportunities for increased sales.Adapt to a dynamic and competitive environment while maintaining professionalism and a client-focused approach.Contribute to team success by sharing strategies, supporting peers, and demonstrating initiative. Skills GainedSales & Negotiation: Learn how to identify client needs, present value-driven solutions, and close deals effectively.Marketing Strategy: Gain experience developing creative campaigns that connect major brands with small businessesStrategic Communication: Build trust through persuasive presentations and targeted messaging.Leadership & Teamwork: Thrive in a results-oriented team environment and demonstrate growth potential.Adaptability: Adjust to evolving client goals and market trends with agility and confidence. This position provides full exposure to the sales and marketing cycle — from lead generation and outreach to campaign development and execution. It’s an opportunity to build key skills in communication, adaptability, leadership, and client management while working directly with senior executives and corporate partners.

jobs.description: Employer: Graham Packaging Company Expires: 09/12/2026 About us:Graham Packaging is dedicated to strengthening its role as a lead provider of custom blow-molding container solutions in the structural plastic packaging industry. We are dedicated to reducing our environmental impact and embracing circular economy principles through our forward-thinking design approach. Location:This position is based at Graham Packaging Company's Global Technology Center in York, PARole Overview:We are looking for a talented and passionate Design Intern to join our team at Graham Packaging. This is an exciting opportunity to work on real-world projects that make a meaningful impact for some of the world's leading blue-chip brands. From beverages and household products to automotive packaging, you will take part in creating innovative packaging solutions that millions of consumers interact with every day.As part of our design team, you'll collaborate closely with experienced designers, engineers, and cross-functional partners to develop new concepts and bring ideas to life. You'll gain hands-on experience throughout the design process, using a variety of tools and techniques including sketching, 3D CAD modeling, renderings, mockups, and 3D printing.A strong eye for form, detail, and consumer-focused design is essential. Your responsibilities will include brainstorming concepts, exploring design directions, creating sketches and CAD models, developing visual presentations, and supporting customer-facing innovation projects.Throughout your internship, you'll receive mentorship from our Design Leadership team, providing valuable exposure to the product development process and helping you build the skills needed for a successful career in design. This is a unique opportunity to contribute fresh ideas, solve real-world challenges, and see your work influence packaging solutions for industry-leading global customers.Skills and Proficiencies• Strong proficiency in design software such as Fusion 360, SolidWorks, KeyShot, & Adobe Suite.• Expert in sketching and conceptualization, translating ideas into tangible designs.• Creative thinking and a strong portfolio showcasing design projects and problem-solving skills.• Excellent communication skills to effectively present and articulate design concepts.• Ability to work collaboratively in a team and adapt to feedback for continuous improvement.• Passion for staying informed about industry trends and new design methodologies.• Exceptional design sensibility for crafting visually appealing and user-friendly products.• Strong analytical and organizational skills with a keen attention to detail.• Collaborative work approach, effective in cross-functional interactions to foster teamwork.• Well-versed in consumer-led design processes, ensuring products align with market needs.• Outstanding problem-solving abilities, tackling challenges with creativity and innovation.• Excellent oral and written communication skills, foundational for effective collaboration.• Organizational ability to manage multiple projects concurrently, maintaining attention to detail.• Having experience in both AI and UX design would be an added advantage QualificationsWorking towards a degree in Industrial Design, Fine Arts (BFA), or a relevant field.Fluent in English and eligible to work in the United States.Include a link to your online portfolio and/or attach a PDF portfolio.Mainly operate within an office environment, with the possibility of some flexible work hours.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Growth Intern at Photon
jobs.description: Employer: Photon Expires: 09/12/2026 About PhotonPhoton is the infrastructure behind production-ready messaging agents — connecting AI, conversations, and real-world actions across iMessage, WhatsApp, Telegram, and more.Thousands of developers build on Photon today. So do startups like Ditto, FlipText, and Folk, and scale-ups like Rho, Minimax, and Nous Research (Hermes).We're also the team behind some of the most talked-about events in San Francisco — the Photon Residency and GoKarting through SF among them — which have reached millions of viewers and turned a developer tool into something people actually want to be part of.The rolePhoton is growing 2–3x month-over-month, and the ceiling on this role is set entirely by what you decide to go do. You'll sit close to the founders, close to the engineers, and close to the customers. If you have an idea on Monday, the expectation is that some version of it is live by Friday.What you'll doWork directly with the companies defining this space. You'll be in the room with the teams building on Photon — from three-person startups shipping their first agent to scale-ups running production traffic. You'll learn what they're building, help them ship it, and turn their wins into stories the rest of the market hears.Use the Photon brand as a stage. Photon Residency and GoKarting weren't marketing campaigns; they were ideas someone took seriously enough to execute. We want you bringing the next one. Hackathons, residencies, launches, things that don't have a name yet.Own a piece of the growth curve. 2–3x MoM doesn't sustain itself. You'll find the channels, run the experiments, kill what doesn't work, and pour fuel on what does. You'll be measured on outcomes, not activity.Open new verticals. Messaging agents are showing up in places nobody has mapped yet. You'll pick a wedge, build the thesis, run the first motions, and tell us whether it's real.You might be a fit ifYou've shipped something on your own. Scale matters less than the fact that you started it.You write well and quickly. Most of growth here is producing ideas.You can commute to SF.You'd rather be given a problem than a task list.

jobs.description: Employer: Nationwide Energy Partners, LLC Expires: 09/13/2026 TITLE: Graphic Design InternDIVISION: MarketingREPORTS TO: Senior Graphic Designer & Brand ManagerEMPLOYMENT TYPE: Part-TimeFLSA STATUS: Non-ExemptWORK LOCATION: Columbus, OH COMPANY DESCRIPTION: Nationwide Energy Partners (NEP) is a leading provider of energy management solutions for apartment and condominium communities. NEP has been at the forefront of delivering customized electricity, water and technology solutions to multifamily properties since 1999. Today, we serve approximately 250 multifamily communities and over 50,000 residents across nine states.At NEP, we empower property owners, managers, and residents with customized energy solutions that drive efficiency, sustainability, and keep rents low while providing financial benefits. Our services include access to capital funding, flexible and fast installation, ongoing residual income, improved net operating income, 100% carbon-free energy, actionable data and reporting, and industry-leading accuracy and reliability. NEP is shaping the future of multifamily energy management. COMPANY CULTURE: We prioritize well-being and work-life balance while cultivating a collaborative, high-energy environment where innovation, integrity, and respect shape everything we do. As an industry leader in a rapidly expanding market, we embrace a fast-paced, dynamic atmosphere that fosters career growth and development. COMPANY MISSION: Our mission is to create a world where communities serve as a catalyst for connection—where choice, control, and sustainability drive the evolution of multifamily energy solutions. Guided by our core values of performance, communication, leadership, quality, and teamwork, we deliver clean energy services that enhance efficiency, reliability, and environmental responsibility. Our commitment to environmental responsibility drives us to make a meaningful impact. JOB SUMMARY: The Graphic Design Intern will support the Marketing team by creating engaging visual content that strengthens the company's brand and supports business objectives. This position offers hands-on experience working on real-world marketing initiatives while receiving mentorship from an experienced creative professional. The intern will collaborate with team members across marketing, sales, and operations to develop creative solutions for digital and print media. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIESAssist in the design and production of marketing collateral including brochures, flyers, sell sheets, presentations, advertisements, trade show materials, and other branded assets.Create graphics for social media, email marketing, websites, blogs, and digital campaigns.Adapt and resize existing creative assets for multiple formats and platforms.Support photography, video, and multimedia projects as needed.Prepare print-ready files and digital assets according to brand and production specifications.Maintain brand consistency across all creative materials by following established brand standards.Participate in creative brainstorming sessions and contribute new ideas for marketing campaigns and visual storytelling.Conduct research on current design trends, marketing best practices, and competitor creative.Assist with event and trade show graphics, promotional materials, and environmental signage.Receive and incorporate creative feedback while managing multiple projects and deadlines.Present design concepts and creative rationale to members of the marketing team.Perform other creative and marketing-related duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONSCurrently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in graphic design, visual communication, digital media, or a related field.Strong portfolio demonstrating creative thinking, typography, layout, and visual communication skills.Working knowledge of Adobe Creative Cloud, including Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign.Experience with Canva, Premiere Pro, After Effects, or other software is a plus, but not required.Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.Ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines.Excellent written and verbal communication skills.Positive attitude, willingness to learn, and ability to work collaboratively in a team environment. WHAT YOU'LL GAIN: Throughout the internship, the Graphic Design Intern will have the opportunity to:Build a professional portfolio using published, real-world marketing projects.Receive one-on-one mentorship and regular design critiques from the Senior Graphic Designer & Brand Manager.Gain experience working within an in-house corporate marketing department.Learn how creative projects move from concept through production.Collaborate with professionals across marketing, sales, operations, and executive leadership.Develop project management, communication, and presentation skills.Gain exposure to brand strategy, marketing campaign planning, and creative workflows.Explore emerging design technologies, including AI-assisted creative tools. jobs.title: Designer at Moglea
jobs.description: Employer: Moglea Expires: 09/14/2026 Position: Designer 8/14/26IN-PERSON POSITION - Part - Time - 20 hours weeklyWe're seeking a part-time Designer to join our Design Team. The Design Team is responsible for various creative aspects of the Moglea brand. Applicants should have a design-focused educational background with knowledge of programs like Photoshop, InDesign, and Illustrator. Experience with video and social media is a plus. Responsibilities include but are not limited to, designing engaging email campaigns, editing images, assisting in planning and producing social media content, and shooting video footage. Our Design Team also assists our creative directors with designing new products for the Moglea line. Our Design Team also plans and coordinates marketing efforts for the brand. We’re looking for someone who is organized, flexible, and ready to bring fresh ideas to the Moglea brand.Our Company: Moglea was launched in 2012 and is under the creative direction of Chad and Meg Gleason. Their artful stationery and product line is created by using hand-applied production processes to add one-of-a-kind elements to each product. The production team in their Des Moines, Iowa-based studio thoughtfully applies layers of paint to extra-thick sheets of paper before cutting them down, yielding completely unique compositions. Each piece is finished on one of their antique presses where it is foil stamped, printed, or die-cut using traditional letterpress printing processes. The Moglea line is a joyful exploration of composition, pattern and color. For each new release, Chad and Meg intentionally focus on adding unexpected production processes or visual ideas to the current collection. jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Visual Design Intern at The Autoimmune Fund
jobs.description: Employer: The Autoimmune Fund Expires: 09/14/2026 More than 100 autoimmune diseases affect tens of millions of Americans, yet the field is still difficult to see as a connected ecosystem. The Autoimmune Fund is building a new way to understand the autoimmune patient journey, and to invest across it. We use visual communication to make that complexity understandable.We are looking for a design intern to help us build one of the foundations of that system: a reusable icon library and visual grammar for The Autoimmune Fund.To ApplySend the following to bonnie@autoimmune.fund.Your resume. A short PDF or a link is fine.A few sentences about why this project interests you.One example of a visual system you designed yourself. A set of related marks or icons built according to shared rules, rather than a single icon or logo. Include a short explanation of the thinking or rules behind it.A quick visual-thinking challenge. Choose one of these three ideas: Immune Precision, convergence, or investment conviction. Show us in a rough sketch, or in a few sentences, how you might represent it visually and why.Section 1 · The ProjectThis is not an assignment to draw a collection of unrelated icons. It is a visual systems and information-design project.You will work with our existing storyboards, presentations, one-pagers and reports to identify the concepts we communicate repeatedly, from patients, diagnostics and capital to more abstract ideas such as immune precision, convergence and investment conviction.Some concepts have familiar visual shorthand. Others do not. For the hardest ones, we want you to explore the question:What is the simplest, most intelligent visual expression of this idea?Your goal will be to turn these concepts into a coherent visual vocabulary that can work across presentations, reports and digital materials, and that can be extended by other designers without losing its consistency.Section 2 · What You Will Build1. Visual Audit and VocabularyIdentify recurring concepts, symbols and visual inconsistencies.Build a master visual-vocabulary taxonomy.Group concepts into families such as patient journey, science, technology, healthcare, markets and investing.Determine which concepts need icons, proprietary symbols, visual metaphors, connectors or other reusable components.Prioritize the concepts we use most frequently.Deliverable: Master visual vocabulary and prioritized icon inventory.2. Visual Metaphor ExplorationExplore multiple visual approaches for approximately 8 to 12 core concepts, including proprietary Autoimmune Fund frameworks.Develop different metaphors and abstractions before moving to a finished icon.Recommend the visual directions that make unfamiliar ideas easiest to understand.Deliverable: Visual metaphor studies and recommended directions.3. Visual GrammarHelp establish rules for line weight, geometry, scale and proportion, level of detail, spacing and optical alignment, containers and shapes, color usage, and filled versus outline treatments.Develop arrows, pathways, gates, brackets, flows and other connectors that allow individual symbols to tell larger stories.Deliverable: Icon and visual-grammar standards.4. Core Icon LibraryCreate and refine approximately 30 to 40 high-priority icons covering the concepts we use most often.Use or adapt familiar universal symbols where they work. Reserve original visual solutions for concepts that need them.Deliverable: Core Autoimmune Fund icon library.5. Proprietary Visual LanguageDevelop a smaller family of distinctive symbols for recurring Autoimmune Fund scientific frameworks and investment concepts.Keep them simple enough to work alongside the broader icon library, but distinctive enough to become recognizable across our materials.Deliverable: Approximately 8 to 10 proprietary symbols.6. Working Figma LibraryBuild organized Figma components with naming conventions, categories and appropriate variants.Incorporate connectors and visual-grammar elements.Prepare SVG and presentation-ready assets, and test the system at real presentation and document sizes.Document basic usage rules so the library can grow without losing consistency.Deliverable: An organized, extensible visual communication library.Section 3 · Who We Are Looking ForYou may be studying graphic design, communication design, information design, visual communication or a closely related field. We are looking for someone who:Thinks in systems rather than individual graphics.Is excellent at reducing complicated ideas to simple visual forms.Understands what makes an icon family feel consistent.Has strong composition and information-design instincts.Is fluent in Figma and comfortable creating clean vector artwork.Can explore several visual solutions before becoming attached to one.Notices details but understands that clarity matters more than decoration.Can explain why a visual solution works.You do not need a background in venture capital, investing or immunology. We will provide the science, strategy, source material and regular art direction.You bring visual intelligence, curiosity and craft.Section 4 · What This Is NotThis is not primarily character illustration, branding or logo design, UX/UI product design, or production work using downloaded icon packs. We are looking for someone interested in visual meaning, information design and systems thinking.Section 5 · What You Will Leave WithRather than a series of disconnected intern assignments, you will have the opportunity to build a complete visual system that can become a substantial portfolio case study.Complex problem → research → visual exploration → design rules → icon system → working component library → real-world applicationSection 6 · Project StructureCommitment: Part-time, approximately 10 to 12 hours per weekInitial project: Approximately 20 hoursEstimated full project: Approximately 60 to 80 hoursCompensation: $20 per hourLocation: Los Angeles or UCLA-area availability is a plus. We will consider an exceptional remote candidate.The initial project will focus on the visual audit, taxonomy and early metaphor exploration. The internship may then continue into development of the full library, based on mutual fit and the strength of the initial work.

Comfortable writing copy and creating content for LinkedIn, Instagram, X, and Facebook, and maintaining a content calendar.Ability to work independently in a remote, flexible environment.High attention to detail, including proofreading for accuracy, consistency, and grammatical correctness.Self-motivated with a willingness to learn and grow skills in areas such as fundraising strategy, graphic design, and multimedia content (e.g., video).Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to contribute to longer-term projects by managing timelines, tracking tasks, and meeting deadlines.LIFT’S COMPETENCIESAll LIFT employees embrace and demonstrate our organization-wide core competencies:Communication: You share information with relevant parties in a clear and timely manner; effectively engage with and present to others; and write and verbally communicate in a manner that conveys understanding of relevant information and issues.Accountability: You take responsibility for the quality and timeliness of work and achieve results with appropriate levels of oversight. You receive feedback in a constructive manner.Inclusiveness: You help create a work environment that appreciates diversity and encourages equity by treating others with respect, listening to, and demonstrating appreciation for others’ perspectives, and using culturally sensitive language.Teamwork: You work effectively with others throughout the organization and promote cooperation and commitment within your team to achieve goals and deliverables.Results-orientation: You focus on results and desired outcomes, keeping team and organizational goals in mind. You use sound planning to achieve goals and get the job done.Problem-solving: You take the initiative to solve problems. You exhibit resourcefulness, innovation, and adaptability to new situations.Don’t think you have everything for this role but are still interested? Please don’t hesitate to apply. We’d love to hear from you! LIFT is an equal opportunity employer and believes that diversity in all dimensions of the organization supports and bolsters the innovative thinking essential to its success and is committed to providing equal employment opportunity to all qualified applicants. LIFT’s goal is for our people to reflect the communities in which we live and serve and to ensure representation of people of color, those who identify as women, veterans, and individuals with disabilities in our organization. WHAT WE OFFER Hourly rate: $22/hour. LIFT’s compensation philosophy is to pay competitively for our non-profit sector and ensure equity across the organization. The compensation range we offer represents a good faith estimate of what we may pay for the position at the time of posting. jobs.title: Strategic Marketing Intern at TADA Mobility (USA) LLC
jobs.description: Employer: TADA Mobility (USA) LLC Expires: 09/19/2026 About ThrooThroo is a Singapore-based ride-hailing platform that has disrupted the Southeast Asian market since its launch in 2018. Unlike traditional giants like Uber or Lyft, Throo operates on a zero-commission model. Instead of taking a large percentage of every fare (often 20% or more), Throo charges drivers a small, fixed platform fee. This ensures that drivers retain more of their hard-earned income and riders enjoy more competitive, transparent pricing.Powered by MVL’s blockchain, Throo creates a "fairness-first" ecosystem. By recording ride data securely and transparently, the platform incentivizes safe driving and high service quality through a token-based rewards system. Having already captured significant market share in Singapore, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand, and Hong Kong, Throo is now bringing its blockchain-backed, driver-centric model to the West, with New York City serving as the cornerstone of its North American expansion.About the RoleThroo is expanding, and we are looking for a Strategic Marketing Intern to join our foundational New York City Launch Team. NYC is the most competitive and regulated ride-hailing market globally. We need a high-velocity, intellectually curious individual to help build Throo’s brand from the ground up in New York City.You will work directly with the Launch Lead to create UGC content, design a localized messaging strategy, and execute the marketing playbook that will define Throo’s success in North America.Key Responsibilities1. NYC Market Entry & Messaging StrategyHyper-Local Messaging: Craft the "Why Throo" narrative specifically for the NYC market, differentiating us from incumbents (Uber/Lyft/Revel) for both driver-partners and riders.Segmented Campaigns: Develop bespoke messaging strategies for diverse NYC segments—from Manhattan commuters to outer-borough driver communities.GTM Execution: Support the end-to-end execution of the New York Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy across digital, OOH (Out-of-Home), and grassroots channels.Content Creation: Create UGC or other marketing materials to onboard New Yorkers2. Stakeholder Mapping & AdvocacyInfluence Mapping: Identify and map key NYC power players, including TLC (Taxi & Limousine Commission) influencers, driver unions/guilds, and local community leaders.Partnership Scoping: Identify and vet local NYC brand partners (lifestyle, fintech, or events) for co-marketing opportunities that provide immediate "street cred" and user trust.Public Perception: Assist in managing PR efforts to position Throo as the "fairer" alternative in the NYC transport ecosystem.What You’ll NeedNYC DNA: Deep familiarity with the New York City landscape, culture, and transit habits.Creativity Mindset: Positive, experimental approach to content creationStrategic Rigor: Ability to map complex stakeholder ecosystems and translate "fairness" into a compelling, high-conversion marketing hook.Communication: "First-class" written and verbal skills; ability to hold your own in a room with senior leadership and external partners.Why This Role?Zero-to-One Experience: You aren't maintaining a brand; you are building one in the world's most famous city.High Visibility: As part of a lean launch team, your work on messaging and stakeholder mapping will be seen and used by Throo’s global leadership.Impact: Direct involvement in one of the most significant milestones in Throo’s company history.

jobs.title: Program Manager Premier College Intern Program at WPAFB Program Manager Trainee Program
jobs.description: Employer: WPAFB Program Manager Trainee Program Expires: 09/20/2026 About WPAFB Program Manager Trainee ProgramLooking for Civilian Program Managers to lead the Air Force into the 21st centuryOne of six centers under Air Force Materiel Command, the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center is the single center responsible for total life cycle management of Air Force weapon systems.The AFLCMC Mission: "Acquire and Support War-Winning Capabilities"Our Motto: "AFLCMC...Providing the Warfighter's Edge"We are currently recruiting Sophomore or Junior students to come work for the U.S. Air Force at Wright-Patterson AFB as a Program Manager in the Premier College Intern Program for the summer of 2027. What is a Program Manager (PM)? What does a Program Manager do in the Air Force?An Acquisition Program Manager leads a team of multi-functional professionals in the acquisition and support of Air Force weapon systems: aircraft, weapons, training systems, IT and business systems at the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC). As an Air Force program manager you will be responsible for managing and coordinating all aspects of an acquisition program to achieve the cost, schedule, performance and sustainment goals of your customers, the men and women who fly, operate, or maintain this country’s most advanced aircraft and systems. Your primary role will be that of the team leader. You will be "the buck stops here" individual who must be able to solve problems and make decisions by leading and motivating a diverse group of individuals to perform as a cohesive and effective team. The acquisition program manager must have organizational and people skills, communication skills, and analytical skills. Additionally, as the leader of a multi-functional team, the program manager must be familiar with the roles and responsibilities of the other team members (logistics managers, financial managers, engineers and contracting specialists, etc.) Experienced, senior program managers often manage an entire aircraft program, like the F-22 Raptor. But as a new program manager, you will more often be responsible for a piece of a major program, like the modification of an item that is integral to an aircraft. Your responsibilities will grow rapidly as you gain experience and demonstrate the ability to handle more complex acquisition programs.These are full time (40 hour/week) positions at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base for 10 to 12 weeks over the summer of 2027. After successful completion of the PM Summer Intern Program, the individual is offered a full-time PM position to start as a GS-07 upon successful completion of a bachelors degree. Pay is set by number of course hours complete at the start of the internship. If 60 or more course hours, you will be paid at the GS-04 level. If more than 120 course hours complete, you will be paid at the GS-05 level.
